prompts: Use case: scientific-educational. A polished landscape Study Buddy infographic for Analysis Reporting Lesson 2.1. Title exactly 'Choose a reporting workflow'. Warm white, navy typography, muted teal and restrained amber; adult learning design with clear readable English and generous spacing. Four equal cards with conceptual document icons, no fake software screenshots. Card 'Word processor': 'Narrative and manual layout'. Card 'Paginated report': 'Repeatable page-based output' with small label 'Power BI Report Builder'. Card 'Notebook': 'Code, explanation and outputs together' with small label 'Jupyter · .ipynb'. Card 'R Markdown': 'Render prose and executable R code' with small label '.Rmd'. Add a clear note exactly 'Plain Markdown formats text; it does not execute analysis by itself.' Footer exactly 'Choose for the reader, the data and reproducibility. Verify every generated claim.' An optional AI drafting icon may say 'Drafting assistance needs checked evidence'. Do not suggest Report Builder is an interactive dashboard, all exports are live, or automated generation guarantees accuracy. No invented numerical data, product logos, source quotations or source metadata.

Use case: scientific-educational. Landscape Study Buddy Task 2.1 infographic with exact title 'From article claim to reliability judgement'. Warm white, navy, muted teal and amber; adult classroom style with readable English. Show three neutral article cards labelled 'Article A', 'Article B', 'Article C' entering one evidence-review workflow. Five numbered stages with exact labels: '1 Record the claim', '2 Trace the original source', '3 Check date, context and numbers', '4 Separate evidence from interpretation', '5 Write a qualified judgement'. Show a compact evidence note card with field labels 'Claim', 'Evidence', 'Limit', 'Verdict'. Add callouts exactly 'A repost is not independent corroboration' and 'Biased wording is a clue, not proof'. Output icon labelled exactly 'One-page report covering all three articles'. Footer exactly 'Reliable for which claim? State what is supported, uncertain or unsupported.' No real political figures, news outlet logos, inflammatory headlines, invented quotes, statistical values, automatic source credibility scores or completed verdicts. This is a conceptual method, not proof that the learner checked the sources.
